A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same worksheet-controlled task and knowledge assistant, renamed from KITA to Genie. The supplied text, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original StarV2 banking evaluation results and a 62-participant user study covering restaurant reservations, ticket submission and course enrollment.

after.justification: v2 reports the user-study results, evaluations on three StarV2 domains and original experiments with two NeMo Guardrails programs.

M1.justification: The core worksheet, semantic parsing, symbolic policy and response generation architecture remains. The corresponding ticket-confirmation action in Figure 2 changes: v1 emits a message after refusal, while v2 additionally calls exitws(), defined as abandoning and closing the worksheet. The expanded parser descriptions do not establish a wholesale method change.

E1.justification: The static evaluation expands from StarV2 Bank alone to Bank, Trip and Trivia, adding distinct task coverage. The three real-user applications and their underlying restaurant, university-service and course-information domains are retained.

E2.justification: v1 reports a single best AnyTOD comparison. v2 Table 1 includes AT XXL, AT-SGD XXL, AT-PROG XXL and AT-PROG+SGD XXL. Section 5.2 and Appendix D also introduce experimentally tested NeMo Guardrails configurations; GPT-4 with function calling remains the user-study baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a four-query NeMo protocol defining success as continuing the conversation and requesting another variable, plus evaluation of dialogue-act accuracy by normalized conversation position. Appendix B changes the stated SUQL backend from GPT 3-turbo to GPT 3.5-turbo, without establishing a rerun. The existing user-study recruitment, instructions, turn counts and metric definitions remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds a conversation-progress diagnostic in Figure 6 and controlled NeMo failure probes in Appendix D. It removes v1's banking annotation-error case, additional GPT-4 error discussion and user-feedback summary. The semantic-error breakdown and twelve good/bad example conversations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D reports ten independent runs for each NeMo query and program. Figure 6 introduces shaded bands without explaining their statistical meaning. Both versions retain the same t-test reporting practice and p < 0.05 threshold for the user-study table.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3, aggregate execution/dialogue-act accuracy and goal completion change from 91.5/91.6/74.2 to 86.5/89.2/82.8. Course-enrollment values change from 98.6/98.1/50.0 to 89.7/92.9/80.0; semantic-parsing scores also change. v2 adds Trip/Trivia SaF1 results of 83.4/92.7, NeMo success rates and conversation-progress curves. The PDFs do not explain the revised user-study scores.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 of v2 introduce explicit formal definitions of dialogue states as sequences of typed task/KB records, including an initiator attribute, and typed mappings for the system components. v1 describes worksheet states mainly procedurally. This is a limited formalization addition; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the novelty positioning to the first high-level specification language and first representation supporting full task/knowledge integration. It promotes the expanded StarV2 comparison, including a 20.5-point advantage, to a main contribution. The explicit contribution of releasing 22 corrected conversations containing 180 turns is removed, while the central programmable-assistant claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new conversation-progress analysis as evidence that formal dialogue state mitigates context loss. It removes v1's explanation connecting unsuccessful course enrollment to missing database information and premature abandonment. The limitations concerning LLM variability, developer policies, few-shot selection, cost and latency are also removed rather than relocated.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, expanded semantic-parser instructions, response-generation prompts and explicit context-formatting details. However, v1's full application worksheets, banking dialogue-act mapping, worksheet-access link and stated 100-conversation banking sample are omitted. v2 Appendix I instead refers to separate submission supplementary material, which is not contained in the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around conversational memory, knowledge retrieval and policy control, adding works including MemGPT, DIN-SQL, SPINACH and Deng et al.'s policy planner. ThingTalk and LLMCompiler citations disappear. These changes accompany stronger priority claims and broader comparisons with existing agent approaches.

P1.justification: The title and framework name change, and the abstract, introduction and design narrative are extensively rewritten around three challenges. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, the architecture explanation is reorganized, and the appendices are extensively rearranged and relabeled.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two columns to predominantly single-column layout, redraws the overview and architecture figures, adds an algorithm box and conversation-progress plot, and restructures the user-study table. Extensive worksheet figures disappear, while the unchanged study-interface and survey screenshots are relocated. New benchmark, NeMo and prompt tables substantially alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens the StarV2 evidence and improves architectural and prompt documentation. However, central user-study scores change without explanation, detailed worksheet and banking evaluation material disappears, and substantive limitations are removed. These gains and losses affect both clarity and reproducibility; the supplied PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
